body.text: Why is Türkiye among the world's top superyacht-building nations?

Türkiye's superyacht sector combines Northern European engineering standards with competitive skilled labor, deep marine sub-supplier networks, and duty-free industrial zones. In the 2026 BOAT International Global Order Book, Turkish yards hold 141 superyachts over 24 metres totaling 82,383 GT—ranking third worldwide by gross tonnage behind only Italy and the Netherlands, and second globally by unit count.

According to 2026 [BOAT International Global Order Book](https://www.boatinternational.com/boat-pro/global-order-book/global-order-book-2026-report) figures tracked by [First Owner's Reference](https://firstownersreference.com/tools/order-book-tracker) and [Yacht Style](https://yachtstyle.co/global-order-book-2026/), Italy leads with 568 units (240,560 GT), followed by the Netherlands at 66 units (107,796 GT) and Türkiye at 141 units (82,383 GT), ahead of Germany's 78,651 GT. Turkish builders regularly construct to Lloyd's Register, RINA, ABS, and Bureau Veritas class standards while offering substantially shorter slot waitlists and flexible custom interior engineering.
How do Tuzla shipyards, Antalya Free Zone and Bodrum wooden-gulet yards differ?

Tuzla Bay in southeast Istanbul focuses on heavy steel and aluminum custom superyachts (40m–100m+) alongside commercial dry-dock refits. The Antalya Free Zone (ASBAŞ) clusters 50+ marine firms building composite, steel, and explorer yachts with duty-free imported equipment and fast winter refits. Bodrum's İçmeler yards remain the historic heart of custom laminated-wood and steel Turkish gulets.

Selecting the right coastal cluster depends on hull material, vessel length, and customs strategy. [TK Tuzla Shipyard](https://www.tktuzlashipyard.com/) and neighboring Tuzla yards tap into Istanbul's vast heavy-metal fabrication and naval architecture workforce. In the south, [Antalya Free Zone (ASBAŞ)](https://www.asbas.com.tr/dunya-gazetesi-antalya-serbest-bolgesi-yabanci-yat-ureticilerinin-radarinda/) lets foreign owners import European propulsion and navigation packages without Turkish import VAT. Meanwhile, [Bodrum yards in İçmeler](https://puravidayachts.com/gulet-construction/) deliver unmatched joinery and sailing-gulet expertise.

body.text: How do owners' reps and surveyors coordinate yard visits?

Owners' representatives and class surveyors schedule yard visits two to four weeks ahead, submitting visitor lists, NDA acknowledgments, and PPE requirements to each shipyard's project manager before arrival. Multi-hub itineraries typically fly into Sabiha Gökçen for Tuzla inspections, then take short domestic flights to Antalya or Milas-Bodrum to audit refit sheds and sub-contractors.

Because active shipyards operate under strict maritime security and client confidentiality rules, unannounced drop-ins are not permitted. [Itinerary of Türkiye](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/) is an independent, client-paid, flat-fee advisory run by its two founders in Türkiye ("Paid by our clients. Independent of provider commissions."). We coordinate multi-city flights, private transfers, yard gate clearances, and independent introductions; marine surveys, build contracts, flag registration, and maritime tax or customs filings belong strictly to accredited marine surveyors, maritime attorneys, SMMMs (CPAs), and customs brokers.
What hotels sit closest to Tuzla and Antalya Free Zone?

Near Tuzla shipyards, [DoubleTree by Hilton Istanbul - Tuzla](https://www.hilton.com/en/hotels/isttidi-doubletree-istanbul-tuzla/) and [Radisson Blu Hotel & Spa, Istanbul Tuzla](https://www.radissonhotels.com/en-us/hotels/radisson-blu-istanbul-tuzla-spa) sit 10 to 15 minutes from shipyard gates and Sabiha Gökçen Airport. Near the Antalya Free Zone in Liman, Konyaaltı, [Porto Bello Hotel Resort & Spa](https://www.portobello.com.tr/en) and [Crowne Plaza Antalya](https://www.booking.com/hotel/tr/cp-antalya.html) provide five-minute coastal access to ASBAŞ gates.
Use this practical yard-visit checklist before departing:

items: Gate & NDA clearance: Submit exact visitor names and company affiliations to shipyard security at least 72 hours prior.
Safety gear: Bring steel-toe boots for hull and engine-room walks; yards supply hard hats and high-vis vests.
Airport routing: Fly into SAW (not IST) for Tuzla visits to save 90+ minutes of cross-Istanbul highway time.
Free Zone entry: Arrange temporary daily entry permits through the host shipyard when visiting Antalya Free Zone (ASBAŞ).
Sub-contractor checks: Reserve half a day to inspect interior joinery and paint workshops off-site.

faq.q: Where does Türkiye rank in the 2026 BOAT International Global Order Book?
faq.a: In the 2026 BOAT International Global Order Book, Türkiye ranks third worldwide by gross tonnage (82,383 GT) and second by number of superyachts on order (141 units over 24 metres).

faq.q: Why do many foreign superyacht buyers choose the Antalya Free Zone?
faq.a: The Antalya Free Zone (ASBAŞ) sits outside Turkish customs territory, allowing yards to import marine engines, electronics, and luxury interiors free of customs duties and VAT for export builds and refits.

faq.q: Are Tuzla shipyards open for drop-in visits by yacht owners?
faq.a: No. Tuzla shipyards enforce strict ISPS maritime security and NDA protocols; yard tours, shed access, and dry-dock inspections must be pre-cleared with shipyard management.

faq.q: Which airport is closest to the Tuzla shipyard zone?
faq.a: Sabiha Gökçen International Airport (SAW) on Istanbul's Asian side is only 15 to 20 minutes by car from Tuzla shipyards, avoiding Bosphorus traffic from Istanbul Airport (IST).

faq.q: Does Itinerary of Türkiye act as a yacht broker or marine surveyor?
faq.a: No. Itinerary of Türkiye is a flat-fee travel and business logistics advisory that takes no yard or brokerage commissions; marine surveys, build contracts, and maritime tax advice require accredited surveyors and maritime lawyers.

faq.q: What is the best time of year to visit Turkish yacht yards for refit planning?
faq.a: Late autumn through early spring (October to March) is peak refit season in Antalya, Bodrum, and Tuzla, making early summer or September ideal for booking winter haul-out slots.
